findings.title: Driver lemma omits the star under-approximation, refuting literals true via the empty sum (confirmed wrong UNSAT)
findings.detail: emitDriverLemma (src/theory/arith/liastar/liastar_extension.cpp:1026-1034) adds the star disjunct only if d_lastStarLia contains the literal. On the first round (the !seeded path at :1072-1080) and on any round before processDisjunct has run for that literal, the emitted lemma is `literal => (p[v] OR h_k)` with no star disjunct. This is NOT satisfiability-preserving: the zero vector is always in S* (empty sum) but need not satisfy p[v], and h_k dies permanently once base AND negated disjuncts becomes unsat (every driver stays asserted forever). Minimal trigger: a lambda whose predicate is unsatisfiable over the nonnegative orthant and a vector forced to zero by non-unit constraints (the constant-zero case is masked by rewriteStarContains in src/theory/arith/arith_rewriter.cpp:1087). CONFIRMED: with `(declare-const a Int)(declare-const b Int)(assert (>= a 0))(assert (<= a 0))(assert (>= b 0))(assert (<= b 0))(assert (int.star-contains (lambda ((x Int)(y Int)) (and (>= (+ x y) 1) (>= (* (- 1) (+ x y)) 0))) a b))(check-sat)` — eager, lazy-subsolver and push-pop all answer sat; `--arith-liastar-lazy --arith-liastar-main-solver` answers unsat. The `-o lemmas` dump shows the mechanism exactly: `(lemma (not liastarEnumGuard_4))` (h_0 => base with base rewritten to false) plus the driver `L => (p[v] or liastarEnumGuard_4)` forces not(L). Note the later exact equivalence L = (v=0) from the isFixed branch does not repair this, because the bogus driver remains asserted. Fix direction: when d_lastStarLia has no entry, the driver must still include the trivial under-approximation `v = 0` (and in general a star disjunct current with the guard's stage).

findings.title: Driver's star disjunct is frozen at emission while the guard chain is shared per lambda: stale drivers wrongly refute literals once coverage completes
findings.detail: The driver references en.guard (per-lambda current stage, src/theory/arith/liastar/liastar_extension.cpp:1033) but d_lastStarLia[literal] (per-literal, frozen at that literal's last processDisjunct, :1028-1032). In the single-literal flow these stay in sync (advanceStage -> processDisjunct -> emitDriverLemma at :1137-1144), and stale drivers from earlier stages j<K remain satisfiable because each stage j+1 was opened on a harvested witness of base AND not(D_1..D_j) — so the per-stage frozen drivers are jointly sat-preserving there. The soundness invariant 'v in S* \ (p ∪ star_j) implies an uncovered cell exists at the driver's guard stage' breaks when the guard stage is ahead of the star stage: for two literals L1, L2 sharing a lambda, the catch-up path (:1060-1069) and the per-lambda `seeded` flag (:1052, MainEnum is keyed by lambda in d_mainEnums) let L2's driver be emitted with the current shared guard h_K while its star disjunct covers only cones up to L2's last own harvest (or is absent entirely, the critical finding's sub-case). Once cells D_1..D_K cover S, not(h_K) is correctly fixed, and the stale driver forces `L2 => p[v2] OR star_j(v2)`, which can be false for v2 in S* needing cones j+1..K — wrong UNSAT. Black-box confirmation is masked by a PRE-EXISTING bug hit first in the same scenario: getStarConstraints caches per-cone multiplier skolems per lambda (d_starConstraints[n[0]], :690), so the exact equivalences for two literals sharing a lambda share mu/l skolems and force v1=v2; with --no-arith-liastar-model-value a shared-lambda sat instance answers unsat in BOTH lazy modes (verified). The new mode adds the driver-staleness path on top; emitDriverLemma should rebuild the star disjunct (via getStarConstraints) so it is current with en.guard at emission time.

findings.title: isFixed-based completeness conclusion is sound only modulo driver soundness; never fires after a user push (divergence in incremental mode)
findings.detail: Re question 2: Valuation::isFixed resolves to MinisatSatSolver::isFixed (src/prop/minisat/minisat.cpp:291-295): intro_level==0 AND user_level==0 AND decision level==0, i.e. the literal is entailed by the user-level-0 clause database (input plus lemmas), not merely by the current context. Since the enumeration skolems y and guards h occur in no clauses except the enum lemmas (h_0=>base, h_k=>h_{k-1}, h_k=>not(D_k), the split, and drivers where h occurs only positively), any model of the rest of the database extends to one with h_k true whenever base AND not(D_1..D_k) is satisfiable (set y to a witness, all h_j true; drivers and chains stay satisfied). Hence not(h_k) fixed at level 0 does imply base-and-negated-disjuncts unsat — the scenario 'fixed via a driver and a fixed not(literal)' cannot occur because drivers contain h only positively — BUT this argument requires every liastar lemma to be satisfiability-preserving, which the two driver findings violate; the gate at src/theory/arith/liastar/liastar_extension.cpp:1086-1094 is only as sound as the drivers. Separate consequence of the same semantics: guards created after a user push have intro_level>0, so isFixed never returns true and completeness is never detected in incremental mode — the unguarded-h branch keeps re-emitting drivers forever (non-termination/unknown, not unsoundness). Also note the exact-equivalence emission permanently marks the literal in d_processedStarTerms (a plain std::vector, not user-context-dependent) based on this context-sensitive check.

findings.title: getModelDisjunct does not verify the base predicate is true under the evaluation map
findings.detail: Re question 3: getModelDisjunct (src/theory/arith/liastar/liastar_extension.cpp:898-992) fixes every atom of en.base to its value under arithModel plus the TheoryArith::getCandidateModelValue fallback for skolems missing from the map. The construction guarantees the returned cell contains the model point and implies base IF base evaluates true under that map. Nothing checks this: if base evaluated false (e.g. a future change makes the fallback values inconsistent with the SAT assignment of asserted base atoms, or arithModel is post-adjusted by another extension), the harvested cell would lie in not(base), the cone would overcover S, the accumulated star would over-approximate S*, and the final exact equivalence `literal = star` could wrongly answer SAT. Today this appears unreachable — the guard being true at full effort plus h_0=>base makes base propositionally true, asserted atoms are satisfied by the candidate model, and unassigned atoms are don't-cares (any completion keeps base true) — but the invariant is load-bearing and one cheap check (`if (evaluate(en.base) != d_true) return Node();`) would make the harvest fail-safe. The equality-to-strict-inequality convexification itself (:948-963) is sound: GT/LT is chosen on the model's side, implies the disequality, and keeps the model point inside the cell.

findings.title: Re-harvest dedup compares the raw model disjunct against normalized stored nodes, so it rarely matches
findings.detail: mainSolverCheckStar's dedup loop (src/theory/arith/liastar/liastar_extension.cpp:1118-1128) compares the freshly built disjunct from getModelDisjunct — which contains raw `(not atom)` literals for false non-equality atoms (:967) — against d_lazyCones[lambda] entries. But the stored node is the result of LiaStarUtils::removeItesAndNots applied in processDisjunct (:1183) before LiaStarUtils::getMatrix (which returns its input node, src/theory/arith/liastar/liastar_utils.cpp:883ff) — negations rewritten into positive comparisons. Whenever a cell contains a negated atom, the syntactic comparison misses, the in-flight-lemma race re-harvests the same cell, and addCone appends a duplicate cone plus advanceStage opens a redundant stage. This is not a soundness hole (a duplicated cone contributes the same semigroup, and the duplicate stage re-negates the same cell), but it defeats the stated purpose of the guard and bloats the star constraints; the comparison should be done on removeItesAndNots-normalized nodes on both sides. Related bookkeeping: if addCone drops the harvested cell as an empty cone, `en.negated = pairs.size()` (:1143) undercounts the stages already advanced.

findings.title: Incremental push/pop desynchronizes MainEnum/d_lastDriver from the SAT solver: enumeration runs with unconstrained guards and skolems, poisoning d_lazyCones permanently
findings.detail: All main-solver enumeration lemmas (guard split, h_0 => base at src/theory/arith/liastar/liastar_extension.cpp:874-883, chain/negation lemmas in advanceStage:994-1006, drivers:1008-1036, guarded equivalences from processDisjunct) are ordinary theory lemmas: minisat pins them at the assertion level where they were sent and Solver::pop() deletes them (src/prop/minisat/core/Solver.cc:1972-1973). The CnfStream node-to-literal map is also user-context (src/prop/prop_engine.cpp:86-90, cnf_stream.cpp:41-42). But the bookkeeping that decides whether to (re)send them is plain non-context state: d_mainEnums (en.guard, en.negated), d_lastDriver, d_lazyCones (liastar_extension.h:449-462). After a `(pop 1)` (exactly the structure of test/regress/cli/regress1/arith/liastar/simple.smt2, which has two `(push) assert check-sat (pop)` blocks over the SAME lambda), the next check-sat finds: (a) getMainEnum early-returns (liastar_extension.cpp:828-832), so h_0 => base is never re-sent; (b) the catch-up loop sees en.negated == d_lazyCones.size() (1060-1070), so no stage negation is re-sent; (c) for a re-asserted identical literal, emitDriverLemma's memo d_lastDriver[literal]==en.guard (1021-1024) suppresses the driver too, making EVERY round silent -> the solver answers sat with the star literal completely unconstrained (unjustified sat, or wrong-sat on an unsat re-query). For a different literal over the same lambda (simple.smt2's case), the driver IS sent, re-Tseitin-ing the stale guard as a brand-new, otherwise UNCONSTRAINED Boolean (its freezePolarity bias is also gone): the SAT solver can set it true, mainSolverCheckStar then reaches getModelDisjunct (1109) with skolems en.to no longer tied to base, so the 'cell' read off the model need not satisfy the predicate at all (getModelDisjunct never checks that base evaluates true under the model, 898-992). processDisjunct then adds a cone for a region possibly OUTSIDE p to the non-context d_lazyCones[lambda], making every later star an over-approximation of S* -> unsound sat in this and all later check-sats. simple.smt2 currently passes only by luck: p[4,4] rewrites to constant true so the model-value shortcut answers before any of this is exercised. Fix direction: make d_mainEnums/d_lastDriver user-context-dependent (or re-seed and re-emit all stage lemmas when the cached guard is no longer a SAT literal / when entering a new user context), and have getModelDisjunct verify the model actually satisfies en.base before harvesting.

findings.title: Completeness detection via Valuation::isFixed never fires when the star assertion is under a user push or check-sat-assuming
findings.detail: mainSolverCheckStar concludes 'every cell covered' only via `assigned && !guardValue && val.isFixed(en.guard)` (src/theory/arith/liastar/liastar_extension.cpp:1086-1094). PropEngine::isFixed delegates to MinisatSatSolver::isFixed, which requires `intro_level(var)==0 && user_level(var)==0 && level(var)==0` (src/prop/minisat/minisat.cpp:290-294). The stage guards are created by ensureLiteral DURING solving, so their intro_level equals minisat's current assertionLevel, which is >= 1 whenever the query sits under `(push)` or check-sat-assuming (ContextManager::internalPush -> PropEngine::push, src/smt/context_manager.cpp:142-154; only assumptions/user pushes bump it). Hence in exactly those incremental scenarios (including simple.smt2, the only incremental regression), isFixed(en.guard) is ALWAYS false even after not-h_k is propagated at decision level 0, and the complete=true branch is dead code: processDisjunct(literal, false, true) is never called, the exact equivalence `literal = star` is never emitted, and the literal is never added to d_processedStarTerms. Consequences: the enumeration's documented termination mechanism never triggers under push; refutation/sat answers must instead emerge indirectly from driver-clause conflicts (which happens to work for concrete vectors, which is why simple.smt2's first check still answers unsat), the literal keeps being re-processed every full-effort round forever, and any case that genuinely needs the exact equivalence (notably justifying a negated literal) silently degrades. The guard-false-but-not-fixed state the design treats as transient ('wait and re-emit driver', 1096-1105) becomes the permanent state after coverage completes.

findings.title: No progress or justification mechanism for negatively asserted star literals; silent rounds let the solver answer sat with the enumeration incomplete
findings.detail: Q1 verdict: for POSITIVELY asserted literals, within a single check-sat the silent rounds are safe: the driver clause `literal => (p[v] or star_k or h_k)` (src/theory/arith/liastar/liastar_extension.cpp:1008-1036) persists in the SAT solver (theory lemmas are non-removable), and emitDriverLemma is re-keyed on en.guard at each stage advance, so any accepted full assignment with h_k false must Boolean-satisfy p[v] or star_k, which the consistent arithmetic model then genuinely certifies (star_k is an under-approximation, so the sat answer is justified); a silent full-effort round simply ends the search with sat, so no livelock. But getAssertions reduces both polarities to the positive atom (liastar_extension.cpp:304-308) while the driver lemma is vacuous when the atom is asserted FALSE. For `(not (star-contains ...))` nothing forces the stage guards: preferPhase/freezePolarity is only a decision bias, and not-h_k can be propagated at a non-zero level (e.g. the y-atoms get decided into an already-covered cell via phase saving, falsifying the Tseitin of not-D_i, which propagates not-h_i and, through the chain h_k => h_{k-1}, all later guards). In that state mainSolverCheckStar takes the `!assigned || !guardValue` branch (1096-1105), emitDriverLemma is a no-op for the already-emitted stage, doPendingLemmas sends nothing (nonneg/split are cached in d_lemmasSent), the theory contributes nothing, and the solver finalizes sat with the negated literal never semantically checked (the extension never calls setModelUnsound; grep over src/theory/arith/liastar/ confirms). The old subsolver mode structurally cannot accept a model this way: lazyCheckStar/lazyHilbert emits fresh-guard lemmas on EVERY round until the enumeration is provably complete, so every uncompleted round sends a lemma and the search cannot stop early. (Caveat on scope: justifying negative polarity via the free-skolem equivalence is weak in the pre-existing modes too, but accepting a model with the enumeration incomplete and zero lemmas emitted is introduced by the main-solver mode.) Minimal fix: call d_im.setModelUnsound(...) on any silent round in which an asserted star literal is not certified by the model, and/or emit a driver for the negative polarity (e.g. not(literal) => (not p[v]) ... or guard) so the enumeration is also driven by refutation obligations.

findings.title: Duplicate-cell check compares the raw model disjunct against normalized stored disjuncts, and empty-cone cells have no record at all
findings.detail: Q2 verdict. The dedupe loop in mainSolverCheckStar (src/theory/arith/liastar/liastar_extension.cpp:1119-1128) compares the RAW getModelDisjunct output -- which renders false non-equality atoms as `atom.notNode()` (965-968) -- against d_lazyCones entries, which store the node returned by LiaStarUtils::getMatrix AFTER processDisjunct has run removeItesAndNots (1183-1197; getMatrix returns its input node, liastar_utils.cpp:883+; removeItesAndNots rewrites negated comparisons into positive ones, liastar_utils.cpp:123-136). So any cell containing a negated atom can never match: the check is structurally ineffective in the very scenarios it exists for. Additionally, addCone silently drops empty (integer-infeasible) cones (650-671), so a cell that WAS harvested and negated by a stage has no representative in d_lazyCones either. Within a single check-sat this is fully masked -- once the stage lemma h_{k+1} => not(D)(y) is sent (same round, doPendingLemmas), any later model with the current guard true must falsify some atom of D, so re-exhibiting a known raw disjunct is impossible and the dedupe branch is effectively dead code; each guard-true round harvests a semantically new cell and the enumeration terminates (finitely many atom-truth-assignments). The danger is in the stale-state scenarios of the incremental finding: with stage lemmas popped but d_lazyCones retained, known cells ARE re-exhibited, the broken comparison fails to catch most of them (unbounded duplicate cones, duplicated star skolems/constraints), and when it DOES catch one the round is completely silent (driver already emitted for the current stage) -> unjustified sat. Fix: store and compare the same normal form (e.g. dedupe on the post-removeItesAndNots node), and keep a record (separate from d_lazyCones) of every stage-negated cell including ones whose cones were dropped as empty.

findings.title: Double 'en.negated = pairs.size()' in the harvest path: currently consistent (no off-by-one), but the invariant is implicit and fragile
findings.detail: Q3 verdict. The assignment appears at src/theory/arith/liastar/liastar_extension.cpp:1070 (after the catch-up loop) and again at 1143 (after advanceStage + processDisjunct). Tracing the harvest path: at 1070 en.negated == pairs.size() == k with stages negating exactly cones 0..k-1; advanceStage(1137) pre-negates the NEW cell; processDisjunct -> addCone appends at most one cone (the same cell, normalized), so at 1143 pairs.size() is k+1 (or k if the cone was empty and dropped) and en.negated = pairs.size() is correct in both cases -- the freshly appended cone is exactly the one the new stage already negated, and a dropped empty cone leaves the count unchanged. The complete=true path adds no cone (disjunct=false builds an empty cone) and correctly skips the update. Two literals sharing a lambda also stay consistent because every path that grows d_lazyCones[lambda] in this mode runs through this same function for some literal of that lambda and re-synchronizes before returning. So: no off-by-one today. However the correctness rests on three unstated invariants: (1) processDisjunct/addCone appends AT MOST ONE cone per call, (2) advanceStage was called for precisely that prospective cone beforehand, and (3) nothing else appends to d_lazyCones[lambda] between 1137 and 1143. Blanket-assigning pairs.size() (instead of incrementing per staged cone, or asserting Assert(pairs.size() <= en.negated + 1)) would silently mark cones as negated-without-a-stage if any of these change -- which would let an uncovered cone's region keep re-appearing in models with the guard true, i.e. a genuine livelock. Recommend replacing the second assignment with an increment guarded by whether addCone actually appended, plus an assertion tying en.negated to pairs.size().

findings.title: Unguarded driver lemmas share per-lambda multiplier skolems across literals (pre-existing root, surfaced by the new drivers)
findings.detail: emitDriverLemma asserts d_lastStarLia[literal] unguarded (src/theory/arith/liastar/liastar_extension.cpp:1026-1034). The star formulas for different literals over the SAME lambda share the multiplier skolems mu/l, because getStarConstraints caches per-cone constraints and (point, rays) contributions keyed by lambda (d_starConstraints/d_lambdas, liastar_extension.cpp:673-731) while building per-literal sum constraints `v_i = Sigma contributions(mu)` over the SAME skolems. Once coverage completes and the guards are forced false, two positively asserted literals with different vectors v1 != v2 that both need the star branch make their drivers jointly require v1 = Sigma(mu) and v2 = Sigma'(mu) over shared mu, which over-constrains (independent witnesses are intended) and can produce a spurious UNSAT on a satisfiable instance. The root cause (per-lambda skolem sharing) is pre-existing -- the subsolver path's complete equivalences literal = star have the same defect -- so this is flagged for awareness rather than as a regression: the new mode adds more unguarded, never-retractable occurrences of these shared-skolem formulas (one driver per literal per stage) where the subsolver path only exposes unguarded occurrences at completion. Per-literal (not per-lambda) multiplier skolems, or existential closure of the star body, would remove the coupling.

result.reasoning: Not a real bug — the claim itself concedes "currently consistent (no off-by-one)", and independent tracing of the code confirms correctness on every path. In src/theory/arith/liastar/liastar_extension.cpp: (a) the catch-up loop (1060-1069) opens exactly one stage per cone in pairs[en.negated..size) before `en.negated = pairs.size()` at 1070; (b) the complete=true path (1086-1093) passes d_false to processDisjunct, whose addCone drops the resulting empty cone (665-669), leaving pairs.size() == en.negated, and correctly skips any re-assignment; (c) the harvest path dedupes against pairs (1120-1128), advanceStage (1137) pre-negates exactly the cell that processDisjunct (1142) then appends via its single addCone call (1197 -> push_back at 670), so `en.negated = pairs.size()` at 1143 is correct whether the cone is appended (k+1/k+1) or dropped as empty (k/k, with a harmless extra stage negating a coneless cell). The three "unstated invariants" all verifiably hold: addCone is the only writer to d_lazyCones and appends at most one cone per call; advanceStage at 1137 negates precisely the prospective cell; checkFullEffort (theory_arith.cpp:292) is the single synchronous entry point with no re-entrancy from doPendingLemmas, and cross-literal sharing of a lambda re-syncs through the same catch-up loop (lambda == literal[0], line 333, so both references alias one vector). The finding is purely a fragility/hardening recommendation (use a guarded increment plus Assert instead of blanket pairs.size() assignment) against hypothetical future changes — no concrete failing behavior (off-by-one, livelock, or unsoundness) reproduces from the code as written, matching the 9/9 passing regression tests in this mode.

findings.title: Driver lemma is not satisfiability-preserving: missing/stale star branch causes wrong unsat (confirmed)
findings.detail: emitDriverLemma (src/theory/arith/liastar/liastar_extension.cpp:1008-1036) emits the unguarded lemma `literal => (p[v] or star_k or h_k)` where star_k = d_lastStarLia[literal]. Two holes: (1) On the first emission for a literal, d_lastStarLia has no entry, so the star branch is OMITTED entirely (liastar_extension.cpp:1028-1032). The under-approximation always contains the zero vector (empty sum), so the emitted clause `literal => (p[v] or h_0)` wrongly excludes the model v = 0 when p[v] is false and base is unsatisfiable (h_0 fixed false). CONFIRMED: `(assert (<= v 0)) (assert (int.star-contains (lambda ((x Int)) (and (<= x 0) (>= x 1))) v))` is sat (v=0 is the empty sum) but `--arith-liastar-lazy --arith-liastar-main-solver` answers unsat (/tmp/liastar_zero3.smt2; eager and subsolver modes instead hit a pre-existing 1-D `mkNode(AND, single-element)` arity crash at liastar_extension.cpp:1202/449, so the wrong answer is specific to the new driver lemma). (2) The catch-up loop (liastar_extension.cpp:1060-1070) advances stages for cones discovered through another literal sharing the lambda, but never updates d_lastStarLia[literal]; emitDriverLemma at lines 1077/1102 then pairs the NEW stage guard with a STALE star (built over fewer cones). When that stage guard later becomes fixed false (enumeration complete), the clause forces `p[v] or star_stale`, which is strictly stronger than the exact equivalence and can prune real models, again producing wrong unsat. Fix direction: emitDriverLemma should always include a current under-approximation (e.g. recompute via getStarConstraints(literal), which is exact for zero cones: v = 0), and the catch-up path must refresh it before pairing it with a new guard. The doc comment claiming the lemma is satisfiability preserving (liastar_extension.cpp:1017-1020, liastar_extension.h driver description) is wrong as implemented.

findings.title: MainEnum state outlives user-context-scoped lemmas: wrong sat after pop in incremental mode (confirmed)
findings.detail: All guard-chain lemmas (h_0 => base, h_k => h_{k-1}, h_k => not(D_k), drivers) are sent as ordinary theory lemmas and are RETRACTED on user-context pop, but the bookkeeping that gates their emission lives in non-context-dependent std::maps: d_mainEnums and d_lastDriver (src/theory/arith/liastar/liastar_extension.h:450-462), plus en.negated and en.guard inside MainEnum. getMainEnum only seeds h_0 => base once per lambda lifetime (liastar_extension.cpp:823-884), advanceStage lemmas are emitted once per cone (en.negated never resets), and emitDriverLemma no-ops when d_lastDriver[literal] == en.guard. After a pop, en.guard refers to a dangling SAT variable with no chain behind it: the SAT solver can set it true while the skolems sit in an already-covered cell; mainSolverCheckStar then re-harvests a known cell, the dedupe path (liastar_extension.cpp:1118-1128) re-emits an already-cached driver, doPendingLemmas sends nothing, and the candidate model is accepted. CONFIRMED: /tmp/liastar_pushpop2.smt2 (check (1 1) unsat, pop, then check (2 1) with the same lambda, which is also unsat since 2+1 < 5) answers `unsat` then `sat` in main-solver mode; subsolver mode answers `unsat`/`unsat`. The subsolver mode is immune because its accumulated state lives in the subsolver, not in the main SAT solver's retractable clause database. Note the existing regress test simple.smt2 uses push/pop but masks this because its second query is certified via the p[v] split. Fix direction: make the per-lambda/per-literal gating user-context-dependent (CDO/CDHashMap on userContext()), or re-seed the full chain when the user context changes.

findings.title: No-progress rounds silently accept the candidate model without certifying the star literal
findings.detail: Every failure path in mainSolverCheckStar 're-emits' the driver and returns: guard unassigned or false-but-not-fixed (liastar_extension.cpp:1095-1105), getModelDisjunct returning null (1111-1117), and the dedupe hit (1118-1128). But the driver for the current stage was already emitted when the stage was opened (d_lastDriver[literal] == en.guard always holds by then), so emitDriverLemma is a no-op and doPendingLemmas flushes nothing. TheoryArith::postCheck (src/theory/arith/theory_arith.cpp:292-298) then proceeds with no lemma sent and the candidate model is accepted -- there is no 'next round' to 'try again' in, and the extension never calls d_im.setModelUnsound. This is sound only when the SAT assignment certifies the literal via the p[v] or star branches of the driver clause; it is NOT sound when (a) the guard branch is the satisfied one but the harvest failed (null disjunct: skolem missing from arithModel with null/non-const candidate value, atoms not evaluating to constants), or (b) the literal is asserted NEGATIVELY (the driver is vacuous for not(literal), and nothing certifies v not-in S* until the exact equivalence is emitted; if the guard is false at a non-zero decision level the round emits nothing). Path (a)+dedupe is exactly the mechanism behind the confirmed wrong-sat in the push/pop counterexample. By contrast, the subsolver mode (lazyCheckStar/lazyHilbert) makes progress every round: the subsolver always yields either a new cell or completeness, so a refinement lemma is always sent until the literal is fully reduced. Fix direction: when a round makes no progress for an unreduced literal, either force progress (e.g. split on the skolem atoms / re-assert the chain) or mark the model unsound so sat is not answered.

findings.title: Cell dedupe compares raw harvested disjunct against the normalized stored node, so it misses semantically equal cells
findings.detail: mainSolverCheckStar's re-harvest guard (src/theory/arith/liastar/liastar_extension.cpp:1118-1128) compares `pair.first == disjunct` where `disjunct` is the raw output of getModelDisjunct (which produces `atom.notNode()` literals for atoms false in the model, liastar_extension.cpp:964-968), while `pair.first` stored in d_lazyCones is the output of `LiaStarUtils::getMatrix(variables, removeItesAndNots(disjunct)).second` (processDisjunct, liastar_extension.cpp:1183-1197; getMatrix returns its input node, liastar_utils.cpp:883-941). Whenever the harvested cell contains at least one negated atom, the raw and stored forms differ syntactically and the dedupe never fires; the same cell is then run through processDisjunct again, appending a duplicate cone and duplicate star skolems/constraints (semantically harmless but bloats the encoding, and the protection the comment claims does not exist). Compare the normalized form instead (apply removeItesAndNots before the comparison), or store the raw form alongside the cone.

findings.title: getCandidateModelValue fallback can produce an ill-formed integer constant (debug assertion failure)
findings.detail: getModelDisjunct's fallback (src/theory/arith/liastar/liastar_extension.cpp:915-927) calls TheoryArith::getCandidateModelValue for skolems missing from arithModel. The liastar extension runs BEFORE sanityCheckIntegerModel (theory_arith.cpp:287-325), and collectModelValues filters integer variables with fractional simplex values into d_arithModelCacheIllTyped rather than arithModel -- i.e. the skolem is missing from arithModel precisely in the rare case its candidate value is non-integral. The fallback then reaches TheoryArithPrivate::getCandidateModelValue (theory_arith_private.cpp:1080-1097), which does mkConstRealOrInt(term.getType(), qmodel); for an Int-typed skolem with non-integral qmodel this calls mkConstInt, whose Assert(r.isIntegral()) (node_manager_template.cpp:1446-1449) aborts debug builds, and in production builds yields a CONST_INTEGER node wrapping a non-integral rational that passes the value.isConst() check and corrupts the harvested cell. For skolems entirely unknown to the simplex the path is safe (getDeltaValue throws ModelException, caught, returns null, handled at liastar_extension.cpp:920-923). Guard the fallback with a type/integrality check (e.g. reject values whose type does not match the skolem). Also note getDeltaValue's AlwaysAssert(d_qflraStatus != Result::UNKNOWN) is satisfied in this calling context (linear postCheck completed without conflict).

findings.title: Mechanics review: ensureLiteral/preferPhase legal, addEnumLemma skip safe, lemma flushing verified, no compiler warnings
findings.detail: Answers to the remaining review questions, all verified against the code: (Q1) ensureLiteral+preferPhase during full-effort check mirrors the pre-existing liastarGuard pattern (processDisjunct, liastar_extension.cpp:1249-1251); PropEngine::ensureLiteral on a fresh boolean skolem only registers a CNF literal (prop_engine.cpp:603-618) and TheoryInferenceManager::preferPhase re-calls ensureLiteral internally (theory_inference_manager.cpp:564-568, harmlessly redundant). One guard per stage matches the existing one-guard-per-round rate; stage guards h_k (k>0) get no split lemma but occur in the chain/driver clauses so they are decidable -- fine. (Q2) addEnumLemma's constant skip (liastar_extension.cpp:886-896) cannot drop a load-bearing h_k => not(D_k): that requires D_k to rewrite to false, impossible since every stored disjunct is satisfied by the model that produced it; `g => base` is skipped only when base rewrites to true (vacuous). Note arith's InferenceManager also silently drops true-rewriting lemmas via the pre-seeded `true` in d_lemmasSent (theory_inference_manager.cpp:58, inference_manager.cpp:36-39), which is what protects the (1)/(2) lemmas in checkFullEffort when they rewrite to constants. (Q3) substitute() over atom nodes with arithModel keys handles non-leaf keys (simultaneous top-down, outermost match wins, matching the linear solver's abstraction view) and is the same pattern as the pre-existing model-value shortcut (liastar_extension.cpp:368-387); failures degrade to the null-disjunct path (see the no-progress finding). (Q5) All mainSolverCheckStar paths end in doPendingLemmas or processDisjunct (which calls it at liastar_extension.cpp:1277); pending lemmas queued by getMainEnum/advanceStage before the !seeded return are flushed at line 1078; the checkFullEffort step (1)/(2) lemmas are flushed at line 356 before any early return. The real flushing problem is rounds that flush zero lemmas (separate finding). (Q6) No compiler warnings: verified with both the clang Debug build and gcc -Wall -Wextra production flags via compile_commands.json -- 'seeded' (liastar_extension.cpp:1052) is used at line 1072 and produces no unused warning. Style nits: liastar_extension.cpp uses std::unordered_set (line 934) without a direct #include <unordered_set> (currently transitive); getModelDisjunct could take const MainEnum&; src/options/arith_options.toml still ends without a trailing newline.

result.reasoning: The factual observation is correct but the problem does not reproduce. getModelDisjunct (src/theory/arith/liastar/liastar_extension.cpp:898-992) indeed has no check that en.base evaluates true under the evaluation map (arithModel + TheoryArith::getCandidateModelValue fallback). However, the unsound scenario the reviewer describes is unreachable in the current code, as the reviewer themselves concedes ("Today this appears unreachable"): (1) the harvest path (:1107-1109) only executes when the stage guard has SAT value true at full effort (:1082-1095), under a complete Boolean assignment; (2) the guard chain h_0=>base (:882) and h_k=>h_{k-1} (:1003) is flushed via doPendingLemmas in the round each guard is created, and the seeded early-return (:1072-1080) plus the fact that a freshly ensureLiteral'd guard has no SAT value guarantee a full round elapses before any read, so base is propositionally satisfied whenever the guard reads true; (3) arithModel is d_arithModelCache, cleared and freshly rebuilt from the linear solver immediately before the liastar call (src/theory/arith/theory_arith.cpp:280-292), and liastar runs BEFORE the nonlinear extension (:292 vs :306), so the hypothesized "post-adjusted by another extension" cannot occur; (4) the fallback getCandidateModelValue (theory_arith.cpp:511-520) consults d_arithModelCache first and then the same internal linear-solver model, so fallback values are consistent with the map, and the linear solver already reported satisfiable (:268-276) so asserted base atoms evaluate per their SAT values; (5) atoms that fail to evaluate to constants return Node() and the harvest retries (:920-922, :955-957, :970-973). Hence base always evaluates true at the harvest point, the cell implies base, and no over-approximation of S* can arise. The claim is a defensive-hardening suggestion (one cheap fail-safe check) guarding against hypothetical future refactors, not a reproducible soundness bug introduced by the main-solver mode.

CONFIRMED REAL. Reproduced end-to-end on a freshly rebuilt binary from the current working tree (ninja cvc5-bin in /home/mudathir/all/cvc5/mudathir/build, then re-ran).

1. Reproduction: with the reviewer's test (adjusted only to use (set-logic HO_ALL), required by the parser for lambda), `--arith-liastar-lazy --arith-liastar-main-solver` answers UNSAT while default/eager, `--arith-liastar-lazy` (subsolver, also under --check-models), and `--arith-liastar-lazy --arith-liastar-push-pop` all answer SAT. Semantically SAT is correct: the predicate (x+y>=1 AND -(x+y)>=0) is unsatisfiable, so the star set is exactly {0} (empty sum), and a=b=0 satisfies all assertions.

2. Code mechanism matches exactly. In src/theory/arith/liastar/liastar_extension.cpp, emitDriverLemma (lines 1008-1037) adds the star branch only conditionally: `auto starIt = d_lastStarLia.find(literal);` (line 1028) with `branches.push_back(starIt->second)` only if found (line 1031). On the first round, mainSolverCheckStar takes the `!seeded` path (lines 1072-1080) and calls emitDriverLemma before processDisjunct has ever run for the literal, so d_lastStarLia has no entry and the emitted lemma is `literal => (p[v] OR h_0)` with no star disjunct. The lemma is queued unguarded and permanently via addEnumLemma -> d_im.addPendingLemma (lines 886-896, 1034).

3. The `-o lemmas` dump shows precisely the claimed two lemmas before the unsat: `(lemma (not liastarEnumGuard_4) :source ARITH_LIA_STAR_ENUM)` (this is h_0 => base from line 882, with base rewritten to false since the predicate is contradictory) and the driver `(=> (int.star-contains ...) (or (and (>= (+ a b) 1) (not (>= (+ a b) 1))) liastarEnumGuard_4))`. p[v] rewrites to false and the guard is fixed false at level 0, so not(literal) is forced against the asserted literal -> wrong UNSAT. Notably the run conflicts out before the isFixed/processDisjunct(complete=true) repair branch (liastar_extension.cpp:1088-1093) even fires; and even if it did, the bogus driver lemma remains asserted, so the exact equivalence literal = (v=0) would just produce the same conflict.

4. The masking detail is also accurate: rewriteStarContains (src/theory/arith/arith_rewriter.cpp:1087-1102) rewrites star-contains to true when all vector elements are constant zero, which is why the trigger needs the vector forced to zero via (>= a 0)/(<= a 0) constraints rather than literal constants.

5. Introduced by the new mode: the entire driver path is reached only under `options().arith.arithLiaStarMainSolver` (liastar_extension.cpp:405-407); the subsolver paths are unaffected.

The not-sat-preserving argument is sound: 0 is always in S* (empty sum), so `literal => (p[v] OR star_k OR h_k)` is only valid when star_k includes at least v=0; omitting it makes the lemma refute literals whose only witness is the empty (or any not-yet-discovered) sum once h_k is dead. The suggested fix direction (always include at least the trivial under-approximation v=0 in the driver when d_lastStarLia has no entry) is consistent with the design comment at lines 1010-1021, which itself states the lemma should contain the star branch.

Confirmed real (performance/dedup-defeat, not soundness — as the reviewer states). The chain reproduces concretely: (1) getModelDisjunct builds raw negations `atom.notNode()` for false non-equality atoms (liastar_extension.cpp:967) and returns the disjunct in bound-variable space; (2) processDisjunct normalizes via LiaStarUtils::removeItesAndNots (liastar_extension.cpp:1183), whose removeNot (liastar_utils.cpp:439-465) rewrites e.g. (not (>= a b)) -> (< a b); (3) getMatrix returns {constraints, n} with n the normalized input node (liastar_utils.cpp:900/920/932), and addCone stores {pair.second, cone} in d_lazyCones (liastar_extension.cpp:670); (4) the dedup loop (liastar_extension.cpp:1120-1128) compares the raw fresh disjunct against these normalized stored nodes with Node identity, so it can never match any cell containing a false non-equality atom (it only works for all-true cells, and false integer-equality atoms which become positive GT/LT at :962 and survive normalization). On a miss, addCone (no dedup, only empty-cone drop) appends a duplicate cone, getStarConstraints (:695-719) mints redundant fresh skolems/constraints bloating the star under-approximation, and advanceStage opens a redundant stage — defeating the guard's explicitly stated purpose (comment :1118-1119). The race is plausible especially via the getCandidateModelValue fallback (:915-927) whose values need not satisfy the queued stage-negation lemma. All of this is new code introduced by the main-solver mode. Caveats: the side remark that `en.negated = pairs.size()` (:1143) "undercounts" is incorrect — per liastar_extension.h:310-312 `negated` counts negated d_lazyCones entries and the invariant remains consistent if a cone were dropped (and a model-inhabited cell cannot yield an empty cone anyway); and whether the re-harvest race actually fires in the 9 regressions is unverified, so the impact may be latent. The core finding and the proposed fix (compare removeItesAndNots-normalized nodes on both sides) are correct.

The reviewer's code-level facts are accurate but the defect is pre-existing, not introduced by the new main-solver mode — as the reviewer's own claim concedes ("pre-existing root... flagged for awareness rather than as a regression"). Verified mechanics: (1) emitDriverLemma (src/theory/arith/liastar/liastar_extension.cpp:1026-1035) does emit `literal => (p[v] OR d_lastStarLia[literal] OR guard)` as an unguarded, non-retractable lemma. (2) Multiplier skolems ARE shared per lambda: getStarConstraints (lines 673-731) caches per-cone constraints and (point,rays) in d_starConstraints[n[0]]/d_lambdas[n[0]] keyed by the LAMBDA, with mu/l skolems created once per cone (liastar_utils.cpp:1045,1069), while buildSumConstraints (lines 133-158) equates each PER-LITERAL vector to sums over those shared skolems. Two literals over the same lambda with v1 != v2 whose stars are jointly forced imply v1 = Sigma(mu) = v2, a genuine spurious-UNSAT risk (concrete example: p=(x=2 or x=3), v1=4, v2=5 gives 4=2mu1+3mu2=5). HOWEVER: (a) all of this machinery — getStarConstraints per-lambda caching, d_lastStarLia, and the unconditional completion equivalence `literal = star` per literal — exists at HEAD in the lazy subsolver path (HEAD lines 666-693 and lazyHilbert's complete branch, refactored verbatim into processDisjunct:1238); the diff hunks confirm only dispatch, the new MainEnum functions, and a mechanical refactor were added. (b) The driver lemma is strictly weaker than `literal => star` implied by the completion equivalences BOTH modes emit at the same mathematical completion condition (base AND negated cells unsat = subsolver-unsat = guard fixed false), so any instance where drivers force the shared-mu conflict also fails identically in the pre-existing subsolver mode. (c) Pre-completion the drivers force nothing: the stage guard is a free decision literal (only downward implications h_k => h_{k-1}, h_k => not(D_k) from advanceStage:994-1006), and stale drivers' older guards h_j (j<k) remain satisfiable even at completion since base AND not(D_1..D_j) stays sat, so the extra per-stage unguarded occurrences are disjunctively shielded and create no new failure scenario. The eager path is unaffected (getCones builds fresh skolems per literal). Per the task's scope (problems introduced by the new mode only) and the default, isReal=false; the shared-skolem coupling deserves a fix (per-literal multipliers or existential closure) but as a pre-existing lazy-path issue.

CONFIRMED real. Independently reproduced: /tmp/liastar_pushpop2.smt2 (same lambda as regress simple.smt2; queries (1 1) then, after pop, (2 1), both genuinely unsat since any nonzero star member has coordinate-sum >= 5) answers unsat then SAT under --arith-liastar-main-solver with build/bin/cvc5 (binary at 06:43 today, newer than all modified sources), while default-lazy subsolver, --arith-liastar-push-pop, and eager modes all answer unsat/unsat. Mechanism verified against code: the guard-chain and driver lemmas are ordinary theory lemmas retracted on user-context pop, but their emission gating is non-context-dependent state: d_mainEnums and d_lastDriver are plain std::map (src/theory/arith/liastar/liastar_extension.h:455,462), and en.guard/en.negated live in MainEnum. getMainEnum returns early for a known lambda (liastar_extension.cpp:828-832) so h_0 => base (line 882) is never re-seeded; the catch-up loop (1060-1070) only emits stages for i >= en.negated so the h_k chain is never re-emitted; emitDriverLemma no-ops when d_lastDriver[literal] == en.guard (1021-1025). In check 2 the only new lemma is the driver for the new literal, literal => (p[2,1] or h_1), where h_1 is a dangling SAT variable with no chain behind it; the SAT solver sets it true with the skolems in the already-covered cell. The -t liastar-ext trace confirms this: check 2 re-harvests the identical disjunct (and (>= (+ x y) 5) (< (+ x (- y)) 6) (>= x 0) (>= y 0)) already coned in check 1, which is only possible if h_1 => not(D_1) was retracted. mainSolverCheckStar then hits the dedupe path (1120-1128), emitDriverLemma no-ops, doPendingLemmas sends nothing, the round ends lemma-free and the bogus model is accepted as sat. The bug is introduced by the new mode: MainEnum and this whole path are new in the diff, and the subsolver modes are immune because their accumulated negations live in the persistent subsolver engine, not the main solver's retractable clause database. The reviewer's note that regress simple.smt2 masks this is also correct: its post-pop vector (4,4) satisfies p directly, so the p[v] split certifies it without the enumeration chain. Fix direction (user-context-dependent gating, e.g. CDO/CDHashMap on userContext(), or re-seeding the chain on user-context change) is sound.

Verified concretely against the code. (1) The dedupe in mainSolverCheckStar (src/theory/arith/liastar/liastar_extension.cpp:1120-1128, new in the diff) compares `pair.first == disjunct` where `disjunct` is the raw output of getModelDisjunct (line 1109). (2) getModelDisjunct produces `atom.notNode()` for any non-equality atom false in the model (lines 964-968; integer equalities are special-cased to GT/LT at 948-962), so most harvested cells contain NOT literals. (3) The stored `pair.first` in d_lazyCones is the normalized node: processDisjunct applies removeItesAndNots (line 1183) before getMatrix (line 1188), getMatrix returns its input node as pair.second (liastar_utils.cpp:900/920/932), and addCone stores pair.second (liastar_extension.cpp:670). removeNot rewrites e.g. (not (>= a b)) to (< a b) (liastar_utils.cpp:446-465), so raw and stored forms differ syntactically whenever the cell has a negated atom, and the dedupe never fires for such cells; it can only ever match the all-positive cell. (4) On a miss, the code re-runs advanceStage + processDisjunct: addCone appends a duplicate cone unconditionally (650-671) and getStarConstraints mints duplicate fresh skolems/constraints (693-712) — encoding bloat, not unsoundness, exactly as claimed. Severity caveat: the dedupe is a defensive guard for a narrow timing window (model produced before the negation lemma took effect); in steady state advanceStage's eager guard replacement plus the persisted h_new => not(D) lemma prevent re-harvest, so the broken comparison rarely matters in practice. But within the window the comment's claimed protection genuinely does not exist for any cell with a negated atom, all the reviewer's line references check out, and the suggested fix (normalize before comparing, or store the raw form) is correct. Real but low-severity defect introduced by the new main-solver mode.

VERIFIED REAL. The failure chain reproduces step-by-step from the code, and it is exclusive to the new arith-liastar-main-solver mode (the fallback is new diff code reached only via mainSolverCheckStar -> getModelDisjunct, gated at liastar_extension.cpp:405-407).

Chain: (1) liastar checkFullEffort runs with d_arithModelCache at theory_arith.cpp:292, BEFORE sanityCheckIntegerModel at line 326. (2) TheoryArithPrivate::collectModelValues (theory_arith_private.cpp:4600-4614) routes integer variables whose simplex value is non-integral into arithModelIllTyped and skips arithModel, so a termSet-collected, simplex-known enum skolem is absent from arithModel exactly when its value is fractional. (3) The new fallback (liastar_extension.cpp:915-926) then calls TheoryArith::getCandidateModelValue (theory_arith.cpp:511-519), which misses d_arithModelCache (same map), never consults d_arithModelCacheIllTyped, and forwards to TheoryArithPrivate::getCandidateModelValue (theory_arith_private.cpp:1080-1097). getDeltaValue returns the same fractional assignment (line 4416-4419) and line 1087 calls mkConstRealOrInt(term.getType(), qmodel). (4) The skolems are Int-typed (mkDummySkolem with the lambda bound var's type, liastar_extension.cpp:855), so mkConstRealOrInt (node_manager_template.cpp:1461-1471) calls mkConstInt whose Assert(r.isIntegral()) (line 1448; Assert=AlwaysAssert under CVC5_ASSERTIONS, check.h:121-122) aborts debug builds. In non-assertion builds a CONST_INTEGER wrapping a non-integral rational is created; it passes the value.isConst() check at liastar_extension.cpp:920 and the harvested cell is computed from a non-integral point (e.g. the fractional getConst<Rational>() comparison at lines 959-961 picking GT/LT).

The reviewer's side-claims also check out: unknown-to-simplex skolems throw ModelException in getDeltaValue's default case (4488), caught (1093-1095), null returned and handled safely at 920-923; and getDeltaValue's AlwaysAssert(d_qflraStatus != UNKNOWN) holds because updateModelCache already ran collectModelValues, which AlwaysAsserts status SAT (4566).

The trigger event (linear solver assigning a fractional value to an integer variable at full effort) is rare but real -- the entire ill-typed-map + sanityCheckIntegerModel branch-and-bound machinery (with a warning message) exists precisely to handle it, and the new mode's fresh integer skolems are ordinary simplex variables subject to it. The 9 passing regression tests do not refute a rare-event crash. Only minor nitpick: "missing from arithModel precisely when non-integral" overstates slightly -- a skolem can also be missing because it is not in termSet (the benign case the fallback was written for) -- but in that case a simplex-known skolem with a fractional value hits the same assertion, so the bug stands either way. Suggested fix direction is right, though a post-hoc type check on the returned node would not catch it in production builds (the ill-formed CONST_INTEGER still has integer type); the integrality check belongs on the rational (or the fallback should bail/consult the ill-typed cache and return Node() to retry next round, deferring to sanityCheckIntegerModel's branch-and-bound).
